title: Affine ideal-fraction log charts and their overlap gluing
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $P$ a finitely generated integral commutative monoid, and $\alpha:P\to(A,\cdot)$ a monoid map. Use additive notation and put $G=P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Let $E\subset P$ be finite and nonempty. For $e\in E$ set
$$Q_e=\langle P,h-e\ (h\in E)\rangle\subseteq G,\qquad Q_e^s=\{q\in G:\exists n>0,\ nq\in Q_e\}.$$
Both monoids are finitely generated and integral, $Q_e^s$ is saturated, and both group completions are canonically $G$ by maps extending their inclusions. Write $\mathbf Z[T]=\bigoplus_{t\in T}\mathbf Zz^t$, with $z^tz^{t'}=z^{t+t'}$, and $B_e^0=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_e]$, $B_e^s=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_e^s]$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Equip $X_e^\epsilon=\operatorname{Spec}B_e^\epsilon$ with the log structure associated to $t\mapsto1\otimes z^t$, for $\epsilon\in\{0,s\}$. These are respectively fine and fs log schemes over the log scheme associated to $(P\to A)$ [def-trf-fine-log-etale-descent-datum]. For every $e,f\in E$ the identity
$$Q_e+\mathbf N(e-f)=Q_f+\mathbf N(f-e)$$
identifies $D(1\otimes z^{f-e})\subset X_e^0$ with $D(1\otimes z^{e-f})\subset X_f^0$ as log schemes; the analogous identifications hold for saturated monoids. They satisfy the full open-gluing cocycle conditions. The resulting fine and fs log schemes $X^0,X^s$ have these affine charts as open covers and these principal opens as their exact pairwise intersections. Their log ideals generated by the images of $E$ are generated by $e$ on the $e$-chart. For any ring map $A\to A'$, ordinary scheme base change, with the pulled-back log structure, gives exactly the same charts, overlaps and log ideals formed with $A'$; in particular this holds for strict etale restriction. No condition on the images $\alpha(e)$ is imposed.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17--3.1.21, printed p. 101; 3.3.5--3.3.9, printed pp. 107--108: monoid ideal-fraction charts, localization overlaps, strict base change.

proof.text: Choose finite generators of $P$ and append the finitely many elements $h-e$, $h\in E$. This generates $Q_e$. As a submonoid of $G$, it is integral. Its group completion identifies with $G$: the group generated by $Q_e$ contains $P$ and hence is all of $G$, and cancellation in the ambient group makes the induced group-completion map injective. Apply [lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation] to $Q_e$, whose group completion has just been identified, to obtain finite generation, integrality and saturation of $Q_e^s$ and its group completion $G$. This permits torsion in $G$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, 3.1.19--3.1.21, printed p.101; saturation finiteness as in VIII 3.2.9, p.104

proof.text: For $T=P,Q_e,Q_e^s$, use [lem-sfb-fine-chart-logification-thickening] for the scheme $\operatorname{Spec}A$ or $\operatorname{Spec}B_e^\epsilon$ and its displayed chart. Its first two paragraphs give an integral fine associated log structure, the stalk pushout formula and the universal property for chart-compatible scheme maps; no thickening clause is needed. For $Q_e^s$ the chart is saturated, so the chart predicate of [def-trf-fine-log-etale-descent-datum] makes the structure fs. The ring map $A\to B_e^\epsilon$, together with $P\hookrightarrow Q_e^\epsilon$ and $\alpha(p)\otimes1=1\otimes z^p$, gives the log morphism to the associated base by that same universal property.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69; VIII 3.3.5--3.3.6, p.107 (chart base change)

proof.text: Put $d=f-e\in Q_e$. In $G$, $Q_e+\mathbf N(-d)$ contains $P$, $e-f=-d$, and every $h-f=(h-e)-d$, hence contains $Q_f+\mathbf N(d)$. Interchanging $e,f$ proves the reverse inclusion. Call this common monoid $H_{ef}$. In the notation of [lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation], $H_{ef}=Q_e-\mathbf Nd=Q_f-\mathbf N(-d)$. Its localization formula gives $Q_e^s+\mathbf N(-d)=H_{ef}^{\mathrm{sat}}=Q_f^s+\mathbf N(d)$. All equalities are in $G$, so they fix $P$ pointwise.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17 and 3.1.19, p.101 (common localizations of ideal-fraction charts)

proof.text:
Here is the ring calculation for either $T=Q_e$ or $T=Q_e^s$, with $d=f-e\in T$. Set $C=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[T]$, $x=1\otimes z^d$, and $T'=T+\mathbf N(-d)$. The mutually inverse homomorphisms are
$$C_x\longleftrightarrow A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[T'],\qquad (a\otimes z^t)/x^n\longmapsto a\otimes z^{t-nd},\quad a\otimes z^{t-nd}\longmapsto(a\otimes z^t)/x^n.$$
Extend additively. For independence of a monoid representative, $t-nd=t'-n'd$ implies $t+n'd=t'+nd$ in the integral monoid $T$, giving the identical cross-multiplied monomials. The balancing relation $a\alpha(p)\otimes z^t=a\otimes z^{p+t}$ is preserved in both directions, as are addition, multiplication and the localization fraction relation of [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. The compositions fix $a\otimes z^t$ and the inverted monomial, respectively every $a\otimes z^{t-nd}$. These explicit formulas prove the isomorphism without embedding $C$ in a domain. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], $\operatorname{Spec}C_x$ is exactly the principal open $D(x)$ as a scheme. Apply this on both sides of step 3: the common ring is $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[H_{ef}]$, or its saturated counterpart.

source.place: VIII 3.1.19, p.101 and VIII 3.3.5--3.3.8, p.107; explicit monomial localization calculation; Stacks 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine

proof.text: The scheme identifications of step 4 preserve the log structures. On $D(x)$ the log section $d$ maps to a unit, so it lies in the canonical group $\mathcal O^\times$ of the associated log structure and has a unique inverse. Thus the chart map on $T$ extends to $T'$ by $t-nd\mapsto\iota(t)\iota(d)^{-n}$. Conversely restrict the $T'$ chart to $T$. The universal property in [lem-sfb-fine-chart-logification-thickening] turns these into inverse log maps: their composites agree on $T$ (respectively $T'$) and on units. This applies to each side of the common monoid of step 3, giving the asserted log-scheme identifications over the base. It also applies to any further monomial localization.

source.place: VIII 3.3.3--3.3.6, pp.106--107 (chart identifications compatible with localization)

proof.text: Write $U_{ef}=D(z^{f-e})$ in the $e$-chart, suppressing $1\otimes$. The self-overlap is the whole chart since $z^0=1$, and the transition to the reverse overlap is inverse to the reverse transition. For a third generator $g$, the common triple monoid on the $e$-side is $Q_e+\mathbf N(e-f)+\mathbf N(e-g)$, with saturation in the saturated case. In $H_{ef}$ one has $g-e=(g-f)+(f-e)$, so after $z^{f-e}$ is inverted, $z^{g-e}$ is invertible exactly when $z^{g-f}$ is invertible. This proves the full overlap-domain equality $\varphi_{ef}^{-1}(U_{fe}\cap U_{fg})=U_{ef}\cap U_{eg}$. Both transition composites on that domain send every coefficient $a$ and every monomial exponent to itself in the common triple localization; hence the ring maps are equal. The log maps agree on the chart and units, hence are equal by [lem-sfb-fine-chart-logification-thickening]. This proves the cocycle, including equality of its domains, for both versions.

source.place: VIII 3.1.19--3.1.21 and 3.3.8--3.3.9; overlap-domain and cocycle verification

proof.text: For each version apply [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes] to the set $E$, the affine schemes $X_e^\epsilon$, the opens $U_{ef}$ and the transitions just constructed. Step 6 checks precisely its diagonal, overlap-domain and triple-cocycle hypotheses. Its conclusions give open immersions of every chart into a scheme $X^\epsilon$, cover $X^\epsilon$ by their images and identify their exact pairwise intersections with the prescribed principal opens. The compatible maps of the charts to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing].

Use the small etale site of $X^\epsilon$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] in a small skeleton in the larger universe [def-weil-size-convention]. The open chart cover is a covering in this site. Step 6 supplies descent isomorphisms of its local log sheaves, so [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] glues their underlying sheaves of sets to $M$. Its morphism-gluing clause glues multiplication $M\times M\to M$, the unit and the structural maps to $\mathcal O$; their equations hold because they hold on every chart and maps of sheaves are uniquely determined there. The log axiom is local: the local inverses of $\mathcal O^\times\to\alpha_M^{-1}(\mathcal O^\times)$ glue by the same clause. The fine, respectively fs, chart condition holds on the displayed cover. The local homomorphisms from the inverse image of the base log structure also glue by that clause, and their structural-map equations are checked on the cover. Thus these are fine and fs log schemes over the specified base. No locally Noetherian descent theorem has been applied.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8 final sentence; Stacks sites.tex Tags 04TR (lemma-glue-sheaves) and 04TQ (lemma-glue-maps), with the monoid operations glued as morphisms

proof.text: The images of $E$ define a global log ideal by taking, sheaf-locally, their translates by sections of $M$; the transition maps fix $P$ and hence all these generators. In the $e$-chart every $h\in E$ satisfies $h=e+(h-e)$ with $h-e\in Q_e\subseteq Q_e^s$. Its image is therefore in the ideal generated by $e$. Conversely $e\in E$, so the two ideals coincide. This calculation is in the log monoid, not in the ring of functions, and requires no assumption that $\alpha(e)$ is nonzero or regular.

source.place: VIII 3.1.18--3.1.19, p.101 and 3.3.7--3.3.9, pp.107--108 (principal transformed log ideal)

proof.text:
For $A\to A'$ and $T=Q_e^\epsilon$ or any common localization above, [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] gives
$$A'\otimes_A(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[T])\simeq A'\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[T],\qquad a'\otimes(a\otimes z^t)\mapsto a'\phi(a)\otimes z^t.$$
By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] these are the ordinary scheme base-change charts. Write $p:X^\epsilon\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}A'\to X^\epsilon$ for the projection. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], with $U=S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ and $V=X_e^\epsilon$, respectively $V=U_{ef}$, the base-changed charts are the open subschemes $p^{-1}(X_e^\epsilon)$, which cover the base change, and their pairwise intersections $p^{-1}(X_e^\epsilon)\cap p^{-1}(X_f^\epsilon)=p^{-1}(U_{ef})$ are the base-changed overlaps $U_{ef}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}A'$. Localization and this isomorphism commute by the formulas of step 4: both composites send $(a'\otimes(a\otimes z^t))/x^n$ to $a'\phi(a)\otimes z^{t-nd}$. Therefore the charts and their overlap maps after base change are precisely those constructed from $A'$; their glued comparison and inverse glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. The pulled-back associated log structure has the universal property of the same $T$-chart by [lem-sfb-fine-chart-logification-thickening]: maps to any log structure on the new scheme are exactly the compatible maps from $T$. Hence the identification is an identification of log structures and respects the transitions and the images of $E$. Their generated ideals pull back to the ideals with the same generators, so step 9 holds after base change. A strict etale restriction of the affine base has exactly this pulled-back chart, giving the final assertion as well.

The statement, stmt_deps and blueprint are unchanged. This is the item's first split; there are no new nodes and no repair note. Step 1: Q_e^gp=G, so the saturation node applies with torsion allowed. Step 2: the arbitrary-scheme logification node's universal property gives the map to the base log structure. Step 3: the overlap identity h−f=(h−e)+(e−f) holds, and the saturated version follows from the saturation node's localization clause with S=Nd⊆Q_e. Step 4: I checked well-definedness of the explicit inverse maps for the localized monoid algebras, using cancellation in G. Step 5: the inverse log charts are justified because d becomes a unit on D(z^d). Step 6: the triple-overlap domain equality holds because z^{g−e}=z^{g−f}z^{f−e}, which is the full hypothesis of lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes. Step 8: the sheaf gluing lemma applies on the small étale site. Step 9: h=e+(h−e), so e generates the log ideal on its chart. Step 10: the tensor-cancellation and affine fibre-product nodes give the base-changed charts, and the logification universal property identifies the pulled-back log structure. Edge cases checked: N with E={0,1} gives the identity; N^2 gives the standard blow-up charts; torsion in G, A=0 and α(e)=0 cause no problem. Fault fixed (C1): step 10 glues on X^ε×_A A' using, without a cited node, that the base-changed charts are the open preimages p^{-1}(X_e) and that their intersections are the base-changed overlaps. Step 10 now cites the existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product, and proof_deps is updated.
